review_type: New clean independent source/key, exact asked scope and coverage-stopping review
scope: Original 2017 base/core booklet, all nine original species including Faderan reverse, accepted original printed components and direct contemporaneous designer clarifications. Remastered, expansions and optional variants excluded.

independence.source_provenance_only_exception: Only the five specifically accepted recovered-component provenance files and source-manifest-listed designer provenance/raw authorities were read. Unused candidate components mentioned in provenance were not used as authority.
independence.stopping_claim_handling: The map claim of two zero-addition walks was challenged against original sources; it was not treated as evidence that coverage was complete.

nonblocking_clarity_notes.issue: The shorthand bidding ships can be read as only ships committed to bids, whereas Q82 explicitly calls the concealed reserve nonbidding. I read the intended rule as ships concealed during bidding, which is source-correct; no material source/key error is established by that shorthand alone.
nonblocking_clarity_notes.suggested_wording: Victory points and ships concealed during bidding may be hidden, including the retained pile until both bid rounds finish; resources and cards never go behind screens.
nonblocking_clarity_notes.scope_effect: Clarify wording within the existing visibility clause; do not add a separately graded reserve-timing requirement to Q23.

coverage_stopping_findings.source: Original 2017 booklet p6, Phases, first paragraph
coverage_stopping_findings.source_unit: All players act at once within a phase; specifically no sequential player turns during Trade.
coverage_stopping_findings.evidence_quote: Sidereal Confluence is a simultaneous game; during each phase, every player acts at once.
coverage_stopping_findings.why_current_bank_does_not_test_it: Q01 requires only inter-phase order, Trade ending and immediate invention. Q08 tests simultaneous bid commitments/reveals and ranked purchases, which is a different procedure. Q24 tests multilateral agreement rather than player timing. Q56 tests the Economy communication boundary. Q66 tests award timing and Confluence step order. No actual question clause or required atom tests whether players must wait for one another to finish their Trade actions. General phase-order key background cannot supply that coverage.
coverage_stopping_findings.consequence: A reader could incorrectly impose sequential player turns during Trade while correctly answering all 83 current questions. That changes access to negotiations, inventions and upgrades and is an essential timing/positive permission rule, rather than a cosmetic case or ordinary printed quantity.

proposed_question.question: During the Trade Phase, must one player finish their trading, inventions and upgrades before the next player acts, or do all players act at once?
proposed_question.expected_answer: All players act simultaneously within the Trade Phase; they do not take sequential player turns to finish those actions.

required_facts.fact: Players act at once during Trade rather than taking sequential player turns.

contextual_background: Agreed exchanges remain subject to the ordinary consent and binding-deal rules; they are not additional omission gates here.
source_references: Original 2017 booklet p6 Phases, opening paragraph and Trade Phase
proposed_question.novelty: General simultaneous player action during Trade, distinct from phase ordering, simultaneous bid reveal, and simultaneous Economy conversion.
proposed_question.exact_asked_scope: Only the choice between sequential player turns and simultaneous Trade actions. No separate general all-phase explanation, proposed etiquette, start-player selection, converter quantities or physical handling is required.

coverage_stopping_findings.required_action: Add a question/key/scope item testing this rule and update the current coverage map; rewalk the sources before claiming another zero-addition stop.
